methods.label: Count possible integer outputs
methods.explanation:
Instead of searching directly for real inputs, determine which integers the expression can equal. Let
\[
k=\sqrt{120-\sqrt{x}}
\]
be an integer. The radicals require \(x\ge0\) and \(\sqrt{x}\le120\), and a square root is nonnegative, so \(k\ge0\).

Squaring the outer equation and isolating the inner square root gives
\[
\sqrt{x}=120-k^2.
\]
Its right side must be nonnegative. Since \(10^2\le120<11^2\), the only possible integers are \(k=0,1,\ldots,10\).

Every one of these integers works: choose \(x=(120-k^2)^2\). Because \(120-k^2\ge0\), we get \(\sqrt{x}=120-k^2\), and the original expression becomes \(\sqrt{k^2}=k\).

Different choices of \(k\) give different nonnegative numbers \(120-k^2\), whose squares are also different. Thus these eleven outputs correspond to exactly eleven valid inputs. The answer is \(\boxed{11}\), choice \(\mathrm{E}\).
